Capture and source extraction are construction stages. Kernel dependencies outside the selected closure require reviewed models. The user ELF/checkpoint provides application code, CPU frame and memory overlays. Fresh-image continuation uses a matching joint kernel/application checkpoint. Runtime execution is sequential with local routing, no host services and explicit functional checks. The pause/checkpoint loop applies only at supported declared boundaries.

Linux uses x8 for syscall number, x0–x5 for arguments and x0 for the raw result. The port declares the register ABI. The slice invocation carries ordinal, number, args[6] and a user-memory view. Results and modeled side effects must match the reviewed port contract. The current guest is sequential with MMU off and masked interrupts.

/Users/al3x3n0/huawei/osrec/runtime/slice_checkpoint.c
/Users/al3x3n0/huawei/osrec/docs/elf-checkpoint-chains.md

Application state comprises the loader-owned CPU frame and mapped user-memory bytes. The kernel record is a 64-byte little-endian header plus a schema-defined payload. Header fields include magic/version, record size, schema hash, next ordinal and checksum. References use declared IDs and offsets. Joint manifests pin the code/archive, application routes, checkpoint generation and parent identity.

Grouped CURRENT limitations: (1) selected kernel roots and reviewed dependency models, (2) projected state and bounded object ownership, (3) static application loading, syscall-only pause boundaries and exact build identity, (4) sequential execution without general IRQ/SMP reproduction, (5) functional QEMU validation without RTL timing evidence. Future directions are proposals, not implemented capabilities or delivery commitments. Extend supported coverage and native model comparison, state/lifetime discovery, relocation and safe points, proven schema migration, causal asynchronous observations and RTL execution with a separate timing contract.

Proposed sequence, not dates or committed estimates. Expand reviewed coverage and differential validation first. Then broaden object lifetimes, relocatable loading and safe points. Reproduce one bounded asynchronous scenario before general IRQ/SMP behavior. Add RTL loading/execution and independently define timing expectations. Quantify capture overhead on supported workloads before setting numerical budgets.
